note: These are optional reading sequences, not instructions for religious practice. Linked topic entries remain drafts until individually reviewed.

paths.title: A first orientation
paths.description: Meet the tradition, a central ethical idea, differences among Jain communities, and two key ways of describing the path.
guiding_questions: Which ideas do Jain communities share, and where do their accounts differ?
How do knowledge, ethics, and spiritual effort connect?

paths.title: Soul, karma, and liberation
paths.description: Follow a conceptual thread through the Jain accounts of the soul, karma, and release from rebirth.
guiding_questions: What does it mean in Jain philosophy to describe karma as subtle matter?
Why is a favorable rebirth still different from liberation?

paths.title: The Jain cosmos and the wheel of time
paths.description: Explore loka and aloka, the traditional map of the universe, and the two cycles of Jain time. These are religious cosmological teachings, not modern astronomical models.
guiding_questions: What belongs within loka, and what is described as aloka?
What do the six eras explain about changing conditions in Jain cosmology?

paths.title: Non-violence, restraint, and many-sided understanding
paths.description: Connect ahimsa and the different forms of Jain vows with anekantavada and careful disagreement.
guiding_questions: How do mendicant vows and lay vows differ in scope?
How can attention to different standpoints improve a disagreement without treating every claim as equally true?

paths.title: Jain stories, memory, and history
paths.description: Read stories of Rishabha, Bahubali, Mahavira, and Malli while distinguishing sacred narrative, community tradition, and claims studied by historians.
guiding_questions: What does a story teach within Jain tradition, and what can historical evidence establish?
How do differing accounts of Malli change the way the story should be presented?

paths.title: Texts, teachers, and living communities
paths.description: Follow how teachings are remembered and transmitted, then compare how Jain traditions describe scriptures and community life.
guiding_questions: Why do Jain communities preserve different accounts of their scriptural canons?
How do monks, nuns, laywomen, and laymen together form a fourfold community?
